newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ousted Cambodian leader to meet Singapore P.M. Goh.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Cambodian leader to meet Singapore P.M. Goh.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh will meet Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong on Monday as part of a swing through Southeast Asia to seek support from regional leaders, diplomatic sources said.
A Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) spokesman said on Sunday that Ranariddh had arrived in Singapore "and will call on Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong tomorrow".
The spokesman gave no further details.

Diplomatic sources said Ranariddh, whose forces were on the losing end of fighting with his co-prime minister, Hun Sen, early this month, would make a swing through Southeast Asian capitals to seek support.
On Saturday in Thailand, Ranariddh condemned Hun Sen for rejecting mediation efforts, saying it would bring about isolation, an end to democracy and a return to civil war.
"In rejecting ASEAN (Association of South East Asian Nations) mediation, I think Hun Sen is now isolating Cambodia by himself," Ranariddh said.

"Now I'm really afraid, we will have again a civil war in my country." said Ranariddh in his first news conference in the region since Hun Sen's troops made a bloody power grab on July 5-6. He left the country for France on the eve of the fighting.
